source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why is raising temperature different from giving a model a larger thinking budget?

options.text: Temperature changes context capacity; a budget changes weights.
options.feedback: Temperature does not set context capacity, and an inference budget does not retrain weights. They concern sampling and available computation.

options.text: Temperature adds layers; a budget enlarges token embeddings.
options.feedback: These are architectural changes. Neither follows merely from adjusting a sampling setting or inference budget.

options.text: Temperature checks facts; a budget chooses more varied words.
options.feedback: Temperature is not a truth-checking mechanism. A thinking budget allocates computation rather than defining sampling variety.

options.text: Temperature reshapes sampling; a budget allocates computation.
options.feedback: The settings affect different mechanisms. Sampling can change a reasoning path and its length, but it does not directly specify a time or token budget.
